## docs/architecture.md

Canonical source: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)

# Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UI[Local browser UI] -->|HTTP on loopback| Server[Wattever server]
    Server --> Runner[Benchmark runner]
    Server --> Cap[Capability runner]
    Cap -->|Sequential streaming requests| Endpoint
    Cap --> Suites[Offline pinned suites and deterministic scorers]
    Cap --> CapStore[Capability JSON and audit answers]
    Cap -->|Optional local measurements| Sensors
    Runner --> Identity[Public model configuration identity]
    Cap --> Identity
    Runner -->|CLI and streaming API| LMS[LM Studio]
    Runner -->|Streaming Chat Completions| Endpoint[Externally managed endpoint]
    Server -->|Optional model discovery| Endpoint
    Runner --> Corpus[Local prompt corpus]
    Runner -->|Optional local measurements| Sensors[Per-card GPU and host telemetry]
    Runner --> Store[JSON results and history]
    Server --> Store
    Server --> UI
    Hosted[Hosted browser UI] --> Adapter[Browser adapter]
    Adapter -->|OpenAI-compatible API| Provider[Model provider]
    Adapter --> BrowserStore[Browser storage and JSON export]
```

The standard-library server serves local static assets and coordinates one benchmark at a time. The runner plans cases, collects streaming responses and optional power samples, and saves progress to JSON. Managed LM Studio uses its CLI for model lifecycle and context/MTP scheduling. The generic endpoint adapter sends streaming Chat Completions requests and optionally discovers model IDs; the engine manages model lifecycle and execution settings. Strata is externally managed: its control application starts the server and loads the model, while Wattever connects to the already available endpoint. Both provider modes use the same helper workload and result pipeline. The UI reads status and events and displays saved results.

Merging is decided from a small description of each benchmark, cached per file: its machine class, engine, GPU and driver, corpus, protocol and test cases. An endpoint benchmark saved as remote is matched through the inventory of the computer that launched it, and joins only after the operator states that inference ran there. A plan lists every obstacle before anything is written; the merge backs up each source, and undo restores those copies while the merged benchmark is unchanged. Consolidation preserves original rows, source metadata, model identities and execution sessions. Known board identities compare manufacturer, model and nominal memory as a multiset, independent of sensor order and annotation wording. Conflicting known boards are rejected; matching strong identities take priority over variant-label aliases. Where strong identity is absent, conflicting known variants remain separate and legacy unknown annotations remain compatible.

Discovery inventories the benchmark client using bounded OS/driver probes. It does not establish remote inference hardware. Generic local-power attribution requires an explicit user assertion. Detected fields, user-reported reproduction settings, sourced compute claims, provider timings and client timings remain distinct. Public result projection removes endpoint connection details and credentials; free-text fields still require review. Result files preserve case/session provenance, and older schema 2 files remain readable with additive metadata. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md), [API](docs/api.md), and [getting started](docs/getting-started.md).

**Connect** and direct benchmark starts resolve endpoint identity without required naming fields. Explicit service metadata and known public API hosts establish detected/inferred service labels; unsupported discovery keeps generic names. Canonical public API routes use stable provider IDs, while other routes use private URL-to-random-ID mappings. Port numbers and model aliases are not software evidence. Route identity and inference-local attribution remain separate.

The hosted browser adapter connects directly to the configured provider after the user chooses Connect. It has no hosted proxy or helper credentials and cannot access helper telemetry or control model loading. The browser and helper use different measurement protocols; see [browser mode](docs/browser.md).

The capability runner shares transport and public model identity with throughput runs but uses separate protocols, storage and deterministic grading. Bundled dataset files are checked against pinned checksums before suite registration; no dataset download occurs during evaluation. One speed or capability benchmark runs at a time. After a throughput or capability timeout, outstanding request workers keep the helper busy even if the run has already recorded an error. Live status reports the wait and clears it when the workers exit. Provider-side termination remains unverified for external engines. See [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

Telemetry has an independent host CPU/RAM sampler and a streaming GPU reader. Supported NVIDIA systems retain independent readings for all detected cards, including board power, utilization, physical VRAM, clocks and available temperature. Combined power sums simultaneous card readings; incomplete sensor coverage remains explicit. Single-request phase windows retain per-card contributions. Concurrent requests share one group energy interval, so overlapping per-request intervals are not summed. CPU/system power remains an estimate with a separate measurement boundary. CPU temperature is read only from an actual sensor: Linux hwmon, or on Windows the optional Wattever sensor task (a SYSTEM scheduled task that the user enables in System; it reads the package sensor through the signed PawnIO driver and writes a reading file under `%ProgramData%\Wattever\CpuSensor` that the helper reads without elevation), a running HWiNFO/LibreHardwareMonitor/Core Temp or a live ACPI thermal zone, polled on its own thread about once a second so the sampler never waits on it. Recent history is bounded; online all-run aggregates preserve observed means/peaks and coverage. Separately, the System monitor samples the machine every second for as long as the helper runs and appends each reading to a local rolling 24-hour log (one file per hour, finished hours compressed, older hours deleted). During a benchmark it reads the benchmark's sampler rather than starting a second sensor stream. The log is local-only and never enters results or exports. Neither hardware discovery nor telemetry establishes remote inference hardware. The hosted result catalog is read-only and can expose both result families without provider access; launching capability tests requires the helper.

GPU inventory and execution placement are separate. Model architecture, backend implementation, cache format and available memory constrain layer splitting, row splitting and tensor parallelism. Strata's native backends can support different modes for different models. A detected second card or a requested mode is not verification of effective tensor, weight or KV placement. Use backend evidence and recorded configuration when comparing runs.

The [multi-GPU communication and placement study](docs/dual-gpu-communication-and-placement.md) uses separate diagnostic protocols and source manifests. Transfer probes and profiled workloads retain their own samples, timing boundaries and profiling-overhead labels. They do not enter the application's normal benchmark aggregates. Study tooling and dependencies are documented separately from the standard-library helper.

---

## docs/api.md

Canonical source: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md)

﻿# Local HTTP API

This reference describes the local Python helper. Hosted [browser mode](docs/browser.md) uses an in-page adapter, not this service. The helper binds to `127.0.0.1` on port 8713 by default, or the next available port. `GPU_BENCH_PORT` changes the starting port; `GPU_BENCH_NO_BROWSER=1` suppresses browser opening. Keep this interface on a trusted local machine.

JSON errors have an `error` field. Invalid input and runtime conflicts generally return 400, missing runs 404, active-run edits or deletion 409, and unexpected failures 500.

JSON request bodies are limited to 32 MiB. This includes capability imports; a suite's supported question count does not guarantee that its completed audit fits in one HTTP request.

State-changing requests must come from the helper's own browser origin, or an Origin-free local API client. Send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json`; rejected cross-origin or non-JSON changes return 403. Authenticated model discovery must use POST; GET query parameters cannot carry an API key or select a credential environment variable. See [security](SECURITY.md).

## Read and control routes

Read endpoints are `GET /api/version`, `/api/env`, `/api/system`, `/api/system/history`, `/api/models`, `/api/status`, `/api/events?cursor=0`, `/api/runs`, `/api/runs/<id>`, `/api/runs/<id>/download`, `/api/preview?tokens=512`, `/api/export.json` and `/api/export.csv`. Pass the returned event cursor to subsequent polls. Exports accept comma-separated `ids`; without them they include all runs. `/api/env` lists the models of the last saved connection, which is empty when that connection was an endpoint that is now offline; `/api/env?provider=lmstudio` always lists LM Studio's own catalog.

`GET /api/system` returns a Unix-seconds `timestamp`, a `telemetry` snapshot (or null), `scope`, `source`, `error`, `sampling_interval_ms` and `capture`. The helper samples the machine once per second from startup to shutdown, independent of viewers, model and endpoint connections; a sensor that cannot start is reported in `error` and retried. `telemetry.t` is the reading's Unix time and `telemetry.sample_age_s` its age. While a benchmark measures power, System reads that benchmark's sampler instead of running a second sensor stream, and `capture.sampler` is `benchmark`. Readings describe the benchmark computer and can include other processes.

`GET /api/system/history?start=<unix s>&end=<unix s>&max_points=900` returns the recorded readings in that range. The defaults are the last 15 minutes and 900 points; the range is clamped to the last 24 hours and `max_points` to 10-4000. When the range holds more 1-second readings than `max_points`, they are averaged into aligned buckets of 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300 or 600 seconds (`bucket_s`); each averaged point has `n` readings and the peaks in `max`. Points carry `t` and the same field names as `telemetry`, with per-card rows in `gpus`; a missing reading is absent, not zero. Empty buckets, and times when the helper was not running, are left out: draw a gap where consecutive points are more than `gap_s` apart. The response also has `start`, `end`, `oldest`, `retention_s` and `log`. `log.mode` is `owner` when this helper writes the log, `reader` when another local helper does and this one serves its log, or `memory` when no log could be opened (the last hour is then kept in memory only). Invalid numbers or `end` before `start` return 400.

`GET /api/system/cpu-sensor` reports the optional Windows CPU sensor: `supported` (Windows only), `installed`, `pawnio_version`, and the last setup's `phase` (`idle`, `downloading`, `waiting_for_approval`, `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`), `message` and `log`. `POST /api/system/cpu-sensor` with `{"action":"install"}` or `{"action":"uninstall"}` starts it and returns that status; Windows then shows one administrator prompt. Only start it at the user's explicit request. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md) for what it installs.

The log is kept in `results/.telemetry/` (override with `GPU_BENCH_TELEMETRY_DIR`): one JSON line per reading, one file per UTC hour, finished hours compressed, files older than 24 hours deleted. It is gitignored, never read by Results, Share, exports or published catalogs, and stays on this computer. Writes are batched every 10 seconds, so a hard kill can lose the last few seconds; a torn last line is skipped. With two GPUs a reading is about 560 bytes: about 2 MB for the open hour and 0.1-0.35 MB per compressed hour, under 10 MB for the whole day. The first query over many hours after a start reads the compressed files (a few seconds for a full day); finished hours are then served from memory.

The environment's `hardware.transfer_coverage` reports detected/measured NVMe counts and incomplete or unverified physical-drive coverage. Transfer captures include per-volume `storage_volumes` evidence and `storage_discovery` counts; volume discovery itself performs no transfer I/O. `POST /api/hardware/bandwidth` includes mounted NVMe volumes automatically and returns `transfer_coverage` alongside the capture. Run it while inference is idle.

`POST /api/bench/start` accepts benchmark configuration and starts inference. `/api/bench/cancel` requests cancellation. `POST /api/runs/<id>/meta` changes label and notes; `DELETE /api/runs/<id>` moves a run to local trash; `POST /api/shutdown` stops Wattever. An active run cannot be edited or deleted. Benchmark runs write results.

Both `POST /api/bench/cancel` and `POST /api/capabilities/cancel` accept optional
`{"expected_run_id":"<owned-run-id>"}`. The helper checks that ID and requests
cancellation atomically against new starts. An empty/non-string ID returns 400;
a different active ID returns 409 without cancelling it. Omitting the field
retains unscoped cancellation. Automated operators can check
`GET /api/version` for `features.atomic_expected_run_id_cancel: true` before
relying on this guarantee. Client cancellation does not establish that an
external model engine has stopped.

Speed configurations accept `hardware_probe_policy: "auto"` (default) or
`"defer"`. Deferred collection launches no fresh transfer probes; a compatible
saved profile may be reused with its original capture timestamp. Otherwise the
run records deferred/unavailable evidence. Capability evaluations use this
policy independently of their generation settings. The version response lists
supported policies in `features.hardware_probe_policy`.

Managed LM Studio additionally supports `POST /api/lmstudio/start` and `/api/lmstudio/unload`. Generic endpoints never use the LM Studio CLI to load or unload their models.

`POST /api/hardware/memory` with `{}` refreshes the built-in OS/firmware memory topology, returning `memory` with `channel_topology`. It requires no installed hardware utility and does not run a bandwidth test. Optional `gpu_index` selects a sensor. With `run_id`, the helper checks matching GPU/driver, CPU, motherboard, RAM capacity/modules and reported clocks, backs up the benchmark, and attaches a timestamped later annotation. Original inference rows and session snapshots remain unchanged. An unavailable probe preserves saved metadata. The route rejects active benchmarks with 409. `GET /api/env` includes `hardware_follow_ups` for pending checks whose GPU is present; successfully annotating that benchmark completes its memory check. See [topology provenance](docs/measurements.md).

`GET /api/env` also returns `gpu_setup`: LM Studio retains its own GPU allocation settings, while a compatible local Strata Control installation can accept a saved placement choice. `POST /api/hardware/gpu-setup` accepts `{"mode":"auto"}` or `{"mode":"single","gpu_index":1}`. It saves only the next desktop model-load choice; it never starts, stops or switches a model. The route rejects active benchmarks. Strata Control defaults to all eligible NVIDIA cards for Flash-Next, with its main/output/MTP card last; its Qwen3.6 engine uses one selected main card. Set `WATTEVER_STRATA_CONTROL_DIR` to integrate another compatible desktop installation; otherwise the helper checks the sibling `flash-next` directory. Unsupported endpoints remain externally managed. Primary GPU selection affects benchmark identity; telemetry covers all detected NVIDIA cards independently and in combination.

`POST /api/hardware/bandwidth` with `{}` measures storage → RAM and pinned RAM → VRAM while no benchmark is running. Every detected NVIDIA device is probed sequentially, with its index/name, independent samples and before/during-transfer PCIe snapshots in `ram_to_vram_devices`. Physical slot labels and wiring remain unverified. Optional `gpu_index` selects which result is also exposed as the legacy `ram_to_vram` field; it does not limit the device sweep. `storage_probe_directory` chooses an existing folder on the storage volume to test (default: results folder). It returns `transfer_bandwidth` with capture time, raw samples, methods and explicit unavailable states. Native transfer probes also run automatically before throughput/capability benchmarks. Optional `storage_probe_directories` is a list of up to eight existing additional folders. Their independent results appear in `storage_volumes`; RAM copy results appear in `ram_copy_single` and `ram_copy_parallel`. Throughput and capability starts accept the same private storage folder overrides. Cached captures are rejected when the detected GPU mapping or recorded hardware configuration changes. See [measurement methods](docs/measurements.md).

Include `run_id` to attach a later transfer profile to an existing benchmark. Hardware class and selected GPU/driver must match. The file is backed up, inference results stay unchanged, and metadata identifies the later capture time. This does not reconstruct historical transfer conditions.

A hardware-class difference caused solely by a page-aligned usable-RAM change of at most 64 KiB can be accepted when installed RAM, modules, reported clocks, CPU/core counts, board, OS, system model and all GPUs/drivers match independently. The capture records this evidence in `hardware_match`; the original classification remains unchanged. Different installed memory, clocks, CPUs, boards or GPUs are rejected.

`POST /api/bench/link` accepts `{"run_ids":["<managed-run>","<endpoint-run>"],"label":"Machine benchmark"}`. It groups stopped benchmarks on matching hardware/GPU/driver, with local inference explicitly asserted for generic endpoints. The first ID is the group root. Each run keeps its provider, settings and measurements; **Open machine benchmark** in Results selects all available members for charts, tables and multi-run JSON/CSV exports. Send all desired member IDs when updating a group. Files are backed up before group metadata is saved.

`POST /api/bench/consolidate` accepts the same `run_ids` and a `label` to store their measurements in **one benchmark file and one library entry**. This is what **Merge into one…** in Results sends. Put the destination first. Sources must have matching hardware/GPU/driver, corpus and measurement protocol, with identified execution sessions. Backups are saved and the other source files move to local trash. The destination retains every result, configuration fingerprint, execution session and source metadata. With several engines its aggregate configuration uses `provider: "mixed"`; `engine_groups` and each session's `engine_group_id` identify actual providers and settings. Benchmarks of a single engine become one plain benchmark with more sessions, as if extended with Add tests. Charts and CSV preserve engine attribution. Both managed and external-engine tests can be repaired directly within that benchmark after connecting the matching engine.

Two optional fields cover what the default refuses:

- `assume_local` lists endpoint benchmarks that were saved as remote and that the operator states were served by the computer that launched them. Such a benchmark keeps an inventory of that computer in `measurement_client`; it is accepted only when that inventory matches the other benchmarks' machine. The merged file records the statement in `inference_local_assertion` (`source: "user_reported"`, `declared_during: "merge"`, `power_sampled: false`) and in `consolidation_history`. Power was not sampled for such a benchmark and stays unavailable.
- `overlap` decides a test measured more than once. `"error"` (default) refuses. `"newest"` keeps one measurement per test in `results`, a completed one before an incomplete one and otherwise the most recent, and moves the others to `previous_attempts` with `archive_reason: "superseded_by_merge"`.

`POST /api/bench/merge-plan` accepts `run_ids` (one or more, in any order) and optional `assume_local`, and changes nothing. It returns the benchmarks in merge order (`run_ids`, destination first: an already merged benchmark, else the largest locally measured one), `ok`, the `machine`, and `issues`: `block` cannot be merged, `confirm` needs `assume_local`, `warn` is informational. Each names the benchmarks it concerns. It also reports the resulting `engines`, `models`, `tests`, the `superseded` count, and `also_here`: other benchmarks of that machine that could join.

`GET /api/bench/merge-suggestions` lists groups of benchmarks from different engines that ran on one machine and can be merged, including endpoint benchmarks matched through the computer that launched them.

`POST /api/bench/merge-undo` accepts `{"run_id":"<merged benchmark>"}` and restores the exact files that existed before its most recent merge. It is refused once that benchmark has changed. `GET /api/runs` reports `merge: {sources, at, undo}` for merged benchmarks.

### GPU telemetry boundaries

NVIDIA helper telemetry samples every detected NVIDIA card. Primary `gpu_index` identifies the benchmark; engine placement is configured separately. Live and saved observations retain per-card power, utilization, VRAM, temperature and clocks, with explicit unavailable readings. Host CPU temperature is `cpu_temp_c` with `cpu_temp_source` (for example `linux_hwmon:coretemp:Package id 0`, `windows_hwinfo_shared_memory:CPU Package`, `windows_librehardwaremonitor_web:CPU Package`, `windows_coretemp_shared_memory:hottest_core` or `windows_acpi_thermal_zone:<zone>`); when it is null, `cpu_temp_note` gives the reason. Combined board power and physical VRAM use readings from the same monitor timestamps; physical memory on separate cards remains separate allocation pools.

All-card history uses scope `benchmark_client_all_nvidia_gpus`, with individual readings in `gpus` and per-card summary statistics in `summary.gpus`. Single-request `power.gpus` records per-card phase windows. Concurrent cases retain one `group_power` interval for all requests, so overlapping request energy is counted once. The global VRAM peak is the peak of simultaneous sums. Historical selected-card captures preserve their recorded boundary; missing second-card energy is not reconstructed. Generic endpoint attribution requires `endpoint_inference_local: true`. See [measurement definitions](docs/measurements.md) for coverage, estimates and exported fields.

## Generic endpoint configuration

Use `provider: "openai"` for an externally managed streaming Chat Completions endpoint, including LM Studio used without CLI management. This integration uses an OpenAI-compatible transport subset; it does not implement the complete OpenAI API.

`requested_mtp` records external-engine intent as `on`, `off` or `unknown`.
It is metadata only: it neither configures the engine nor adds a parameter to
Chat Completions. Check `GET /api/version` for
`features.external_requested_mtp_metadata: true` before depending on its
retention. Effective MTP remains unknown without control-plane evidence;
per-request draft counters are recorded separately when supplied by the server.

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint_base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1",
  "endpoint_api_key": "<key, if the endpoint requires one>",
  "endpoint_inference_local": true,
  "models": ["<served-model-id>"],
  "sizes": [512, 5000],
  "concurrency_levels": [1],
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "repeats": 2,
  "reproducibility": {
    "quantization": "IQ3_S",
    "context_tokens": 32768,
    "kv_cache_dtype": "int8"
  }
}
```

Send this to `POST /api/bench/start` only when ready to run inference. Omit `endpoint_api_key` if authentication is unnecessary. The key is sent to the endpoint as a Bearer token and held in memory only: it is not written to benchmark files, the saved form, exports or recorded errors, so every request that needs it (`/api/endpoint/check`, start, extend, capability start) carries it again. A pasted `Bearer ` prefix is ignored; a key must be printable text without spaces. A script can instead set `endpoint_api_key_env` to the name of an environment variable defined before the helper started. URLs must use HTTP(S) without embedded credentials, query or fragment. A root URL gets `/v1`; an explicit API path is preserved. Do not supply `/chat/completions` or `/models` as the base.

`endpoint_inference_local` defaults to **false**, including for loopback addresses. Set it true only when inference executes on the benchmark computer. This user assertion permits local power attribution; neither route-origin detection nor a display name verifies server hardware.

`endpoint_reasoning_effort` defaults to null in the throughput API, which omits the request field. The UI defaults **Requested reasoning** to **None**. Set the API field to `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh` to request standard Chat Completions `reasoning_effort`. Unsupported requests fail visibly. The requested value is recorded separately from the engine's unverified effective behavior. Short budgets may otherwise end during hidden reasoning before a visible answer appears.

`token_limit_field` selects `max_tokens` (default) or `max_completion_tokens`. Explicit `temperature: null` omits that parameter; numeric values request the specified temperature, with UI default 0. Keep parameter choices consistent across comparisons. These are request controls, not verification of server behavior.

`POST /api/endpoint/check` accepts these connection fields and probes discovery without running inference. It returns `ok`, `models`, `manual_model_ids: true`, `provider`, resolved `endpoint_identity`, and an `error` on discovery failure. `helper_lmstudio: true` means the address is the LM Studio on this computer that the helper's `lms` CLI controls (no API key, LM Studio's port, every served ID in LM Studio's catalog): benchmark it with `provider: "lmstudio"` to choose context, GPU placement and MTP. Exact served model IDs can always be supplied in `models`; discovery alone does not verify streaming inference or usage reporting. `GET /api/models?provider=openai&endpoint_base_url=...` is also available without credential forwarding; use POST for authenticated discovery and to keep connection details out of URL histories.

Discovered models preserve safe endpoint-reported quantization, context and state metadata. Managed LM Studio also uses its native model catalog to capture separately labeled `quantization_method` (QAT, QAD or UD when reported), with `quantization_method_source`. Result rows and optional quantization identity fields `method`/`method_source` retain these labels independently of the storage format. Older identities without method fields remain valid. When quantization appears only in a recognized model-ID suffix, `quantization_source` is `model_identifier`; explicit endpoint metadata uses `endpoint_reported`. An inferred suffix does not verify the served weights. Unknown quantization or context stays unknown. The UI uses a manual model ID only when discovery returns no models.

Results uses the current connection when discovering models for additional tests. With a generic endpoint, **Review new benchmark** opens the current served-model catalog and stages a separate run in Benchmarks; it does not modify historical measurements or start inference. Managed LM Studio retains same-file extension. Switching connection invalidates an open or cached model selection. Historical chart filters describe saved measurements, rather than the endpoint's current inventory.

The inference engine controls loaded models, context/KV allocation, quantization, placement, reasoning and speculative decoding. Effective generic settings use `context_policy` and `gpu_offload` of `provider_managed`, with no fallback reload. Result states such as `mtp`, `context_length` and `reasoning_disabled` remain unknown. The helper cannot launch an endpoint's model with MTP: `mtp_modes` of `["off", "on"]` runs the standard pass only and records `measurement_scope.mtp_pass` as requested but not run, and `["on"]` alone is rejected with 400. A client context estimate does not prove the engine's context setting. Same-file additions and repairs require a fresh connection matching the saved external engine; separate-file resume is managed LM Studio only. Cancellation aborts client work but cannot verify provider-side termination; a timeout stops the run for operator inspection.

Optional `reproducibility` fields are `engine`, `engine_version`, `model_revision`, `quantization`, `context_tokens`, `kv_cache_dtype` and `mtp_draft_tokens`. Results mark these `user_reported`. Optional `performance_claims` entries contain `precision` (`FP4`, `INT4`, `FP8`, `INT8`, `FP16`, `BF16`, `FP32`), finite non-negative `value`, `unit`, `kind` (`advertised_peak`, `measured`, `estimate`), `sparsity` (`dense`, `sparse`, `unknown`), `execution_path` and `source`. Source and execution path are required. Use `TOPS` for integer precision and `TFLOP/s` for floating point. These annotations stay separate from detected hardware and Wattever measurements; see [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

Endpoint URL, credential variable name and credentials are excluded from public results and exports. Connection configuration is not persisted for generic resume. Review public free-text labels, notes, model names and sources before sharing; see [security](SECURITY.md).

### Automatic endpoint identity

No endpoint label or public ID is required. Connect and direct API starts resolve them automatically. Optional `endpoint_name_override` supplies one public display name; leave it empty to use detection. Legacy `endpoint_id`/`endpoint_label` configuration remains accepted as an operator override.

Identity uses recognized official public cloud hosts or explicit service/backend metadata. Local/private `/health`, `/props` and `/version` probes are read-only and bounded by an overall deadline; unsupported probes fall back without guessing from ports or model aliases. Unknown software receives a **Local endpoint**, **Private endpoint** or **Remote endpoint** name. `endpoint_identity` records `id`, `label`, `source`, `service`, `version`, `location`, `route_registry` and `evidence`. Explicit service metadata is `detected`; recognized cloud hosts and the declared managed LM Studio provider are `inferred`; optional naming overrides are `operator_override`; unsupported detection stays `unknown`. Location describes the route origin, not verified inference hardware.

Canonical known public API routes use stable public provider IDs for community aggregation. Other routes, including custom paths on recognized cloud hosts, receive random opaque IDs stable for the operational base URL in a private local registry. The helper stores that mapping in ignored `results/.endpoint-routes.json`; browser mode uses local storage. URLs are neither hashed into public IDs nor included in public configuration fingerprints. Do not share the registry. Removing it or clearing browser storage can generate a new identity for a privately mapped route. A cloud provider label identifies the public service, not its underlying inference engine or weights.

Optional `canonical_model_id`, `model_source`, `reported_reasoning` and `reported_mtp` (`on`, `off`, `unknown`) describe the model separately. They feed `model_configuration`/`configuration_id` with endpoint identity; requested, reported and verified effective values stay distinct. Historical `user_reported` endpoint provenance remains supported. Hashes verify content consistency, not endpoint authenticity or actual served weights.

## Capability routes

Capability evaluation and validated imports are helper-only; hosted mode provides a shared read/export/compare library. It uses separate files and a sequential request protocol described in [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/capabilities/suites` | Suite metadata, versions, digests and question counts |
| `GET /api/capabilities/status` | Running state, live item progress and available local telemetry |
| `GET /api/capabilities/events?cursor=0` | Bounded event stream snapshot and next cursor |
| `GET /api/capabilities/runs` | Capability run summaries |
| `GET /api/capabilities/runs/<id>` | Full saved run |
| `GET /api/capabilities/runs/<id>/download` | Public audit JSON download |
| `GET /api/capabilities/export.json?ids=<id>,<id>` | Public `capability_runs` bundle; omitted IDs selects all |
| `POST /api/capabilities/start` | Validate configuration, save run and start inference |
| `POST /api/capabilities/cancel` | Abort client work; provider termination remains unverified |
| `POST /api/capabilities/import` | Validate/re-score one run or a `capability_runs` bundle and save it |

`GET /api/capabilities/suites` also returns `runner` metadata from the running helper process: its `completion_policy`, generation/deadline `defaults`, and accepted `limits`. The UI requires a supported completion policy before launching or validating imports. An older helper can still expose saved results for browsing, but must be relaunched to apply updated capability code; refreshing browser assets alone does not update Python code.

Example start configuration:

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint_base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1",
  "model": "<served-model-id>",
  "suite_id": "gsm8k-test-chat-v1",
  "sample_size": 50,
  "repeats": 1,
  "seed": 0,
  "temperature": 0,
  "top_p": 1,
  "endpoint_reasoning_effort": "none",
  "max_tokens": 32768,
  "timeout_s": 0,
  "endpoint_inference_local": false
}
```

A model ID is required; endpoint naming/identity is resolved automatically for direct starts as well as the UI. `sample_size: 0` selects the full suite; a positive value selects a deterministic seeded subset, capped by suite size. Defaults are Core v1, 24 questions, one repeat, a 32,768-token total generation budget and no wall-clock deadline (`timeout_s: 0`), question-selection seed 0, temperature 0, omitted top-p and requested reasoning `none`. `send_seed` defaults false; true additionally sends `seed + repeat` to the generation API. Null top-p/temperature omit those parameters. Capability `token_limit_field` defaults to `max_tokens`; `max_completion_tokens` is an explicit alternative for endpoints requiring it. Unsupported parameters are visible failures, not silently retried with different sampling. The capability budget includes reasoning plus final output, and is independent of speed-test generation settings. `max_tokens` accepts 1 to 131,072; `timeout_s` accepts 0 to 86,400 seconds, with 0 meaning no wall-clock deadline. Stop remains available. Context and provider limits can still terminate generation. New evaluations record `completion_policy: "finished-stream-visible-answer-v2"`; the policy is part of the evaluation fingerprint. Historical runs without this field remain readable and retain their recorded decisions.

Only one speed or capability run may execute at a time; conflicting starts/imports return 409. Capability tests do not load/unload models for either provider. Local telemetry requires explicit `endpoint_inference_local: true` for both. Outstanding requests after timeout/cancellation continue to block new benchmarks until their client workers exit; `/api/status` reports that wait. External engine cancellation remains unverified, and Wattever does not terminate the external engine. Import recomputes summary/grades from full audit answers and validates hashes; it does not authenticate the reported model or operator.

## Managed LM Studio configuration

The default provider is `lmstudio`. `LMS_BASE_URL` selects its API (default `http://127.0.0.1:1234`). Explicit environment/configuration URLs remain unchanged; historical timings are not adjusted for connection-address differences. For example:

```json
{"models":["<installed-model-id>"],"sizes":[512,5000],"concurrency_levels":[1,2],"max_tokens":256,"repeats":1}
```

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `sizes` | 512, 5000, 10000, 20000, 40000 |
| `concurrency_levels`, `repeats`, `max_tokens` | `[1]`, 1, 256 |
| `gpu_offload`, `fallback_on_failure`, `stop_model_after_failure` | `max`, true, true |
| `context_policy`, `context_headroom`, `context_safety_fraction` | `per_test`, 512, 0.05 |
| `mtp_modes`, `warmup`, `disable_thinking` | `["off"]`, true, true |
| `load_timeout_s`, `per_test_timeout_s`, `power_interval_ms` | 900, 1800, 150 |
| `gpu_index` | 0 (primary GPU identity; all detected NVIDIA GPUs are monitored) |

`gpu_offload` accepts `max`, `auto`, `off` or a fraction from `0.0` to `1.0`. With `fallback_on_failure: true`, a managed load that fails is retried as `auto`, then `0.5`, then `off`, and each result's `gpu_offload` holds the placement that loaded. Send `fallback_on_failure: false` to record a load that does not fit as a failure at the requested placement. See [automatic fallbacks and substitutions](docs/measurements.md#automatic-fallbacks-and-substitutions).

## Model additions, repairs and removal

`GET /api/bench/extend-plan?run_id=<id>` supplies managed extension options. For an external endpoint, use `POST /api/bench/extend-options` with `run_id` and a `connection` object containing fresh endpoint configuration. It returns the catalog, saved execution `config` and optional `engine_group_id`. Include the same connection and group ID in preview/start requests; keep connection credentials out of URLs. `POST /api/bench/extend-plan` previews a selection such as:

```json
{"run_id":"<run-id>","model_modes":{"<installed-model-id>":["off","on"]},"sizes":[512,5000],"concurrency_levels":[1,2],"repeats":2,"retry_failed":false,"rerun_existing":false}
```

Optional booleans `fallback_on_failure` and `skip_after_timeout` control the new session's load-placement fallback and practical timeout skipping. Timeout-based skips are not hard capacity/OOM claims. Optional `per_test_timeout_s` sets the new execution session's timeout (integer 1 through 7200). Existing measurements retain their recorded budgets. `repeats` is the desired total per case (saved repeat count through 100). Raising it adds new slots. To repair individual cases, optionally supply `selected_cases` as a nonempty array of `[model_id, mtp_boolean, concurrency, target_tokens, zero_based_repeat]` tuples within the selected workload. For example, `[["<installed-model-id>",false,2,5000,0]]` with `rerun_existing: true` replaces only that first repeat. Omit `selected_cases` to use the full selection. Case selection applies only to the execution session; the benchmark keeps its full workload configuration.

Review counts and warnings before submitting the selection to `POST /api/bench/extend`. Defaults add missing cases; `retry_failed` includes failed and skipped cases; `rerun_existing` includes successful selected cases. Extension takes a history snapshot and modifies the existing file. `POST /api/bench/resume` with `run_id` creates a separate run for unfinished managed work; an endpoint benchmark continues in its own file through `/api/bench/extend` with a fresh `connection`. `GET /api/runs` and `/api/status` report `error` and `remaining_tests` for a benchmark that stopped early. On an external endpoint a failed row can carry `fail_kind` `model_unavailable` (the endpoint refused the model; its other tests are skipped) or `endpoint_unreachable` (the endpoint disappeared; the run stopped), with `endpoint_check: {verdict, http_status}`. Managed operations load/unload models. External extensions never load/unload models, use only `["off"]` scheduling modes with provider-controlled MTP, and require a fresh matching endpoint connection. Adding a first external engine upgrades the existing file with execution groups. Use distinct served model IDs for variants across engines. All extensions require compatible hardware, GPU/driver and corpus; managed extensions additionally check LM Studio version; see [measurements](docs/measurements.md) and [architecture](docs/architecture.md).

`POST /api/runs/<id>/models/delete` with `{"models":["<model-id>"]}` removes selected models, their results and planned workloads from that benchmark. Other models are preserved. It creates a history backup and returns `run`, `removed_measurements` and `backup_created`. Active work blocks removal. The last model requires whole-benchmark deletion.

A saved `storage_comparison` with protocol `wattever-storage-comparison-v1` can retain frozen `baseline_results`, `alternate_results`, condition labels, paired summary `rows` and cache notes. Both measurement arrays use ordinary result-row fields and stay separate from the primary `results` matrix. JSON exports retain them; Results provides a dedicated comparison CSV.

---

## docs/faq.md

Canonical source: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md)

# FAQ

## Can I run without installing Wattever?

Yes. The hosted [browser mode](docs/browser.md) connects directly to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The endpoint and browser must allow the connection. The Python helper supports generic endpoints without LM Studio, including same-file additions and repairs after reconnecting. Automatic model loading and separate-file resume are specific to managed LM Studio.

## Does the selected GPU determine where inference runs?

No. Primary GPU identifies the benchmark; NVIDIA helper telemetry monitors every detected NVIDIA card independently and in combination. Configure placement in the inference engine and record the setup in notes. Generic endpoints require an explicit local-inference assertion before attributing client power to inference. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Are power numbers comparable?

GPU board and SoC rail measurements have different boundaries. New NVIDIA runs include all detected NVIDIA boards, while historical selected-card runs retain their original boundary. Estimated whole-system power adds CPU and other-system estimates once and is not a wall meter. Compare like sources and settings.

## Can I compare old and new files?

Older files remain readable. Compare protocol, model, corpus, settings, context planner and session provenance; legacy and newer context allocation can differ within an extended benchmark. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Does a failed case invalidate the benchmark?

No. Failures and skipped cases are recorded and can be retried. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) for common causes.

## Why does a result show placement `0.5` or `off` when I chose Prefer GPU?

The model did not load fully on the GPU, and **Use CPU memory if needed** loaded it with fewer GPU layers. The result records the placement that loaded, and its speed describes that placement. Compare it only with rows that have the same placement, or turn the option off to measure GPU capacity alone. See [automatic fallbacks and substitutions](docs/measurements.md#automatic-fallbacks-and-substitutions).

## Must a benchmark be complete before I share it?

No. Partial sessions are useful contributions. Helper runs can add missing cases to the same file later, subject to compatibility checks. External engines require reconnecting the saved endpoint and operator model loading; browser experiments use new runs. See [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md).

## Does any OpenAI-compatible API work?

The required surface is streaming Chat Completions. `/models` discovery is optional because you can enter exact served IDs manually. Missing usage counts leave generic token throughput unavailable. Responses, embeddings, image and audio APIs are not benchmarked. Configure context, KV cache, quantization and MTP in your engine; Wattever's generic adapter does not control them.

## Why can longer prompts show higher prefill throughput?

The displayed metric divides prompt tokens by client TTFT, which includes fixed overhead, queueing and network time. Larger batches can also use hardware more efficiently. Cache reuse and provider warm state can change it further. Inspect separately reported engine timings and cache usage; missing cache data does not establish a cold run.

## Does Wattever measure bandwidth and TFLOPS?

The helper measures RAM-copy payload throughput, sequential storage reads and pinned RAM → VRAM transfers for each detected NVIDIA card. The device paths are measured sequentially; adding their individual rates does not establish simultaneous throughput. PCIe snapshots can downshift while idle, and the encoding-based PCIe ceiling remains theoretical. These probes do not establish peak DRAM bandwidth, GPU-to-GPU bandwidth or arithmetic TFLOPS. Optional sourced, precision-specific compute claims are user-reported and stay separate from detected fields; quantized weight storage does not establish arithmetic precision. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Are GSM8K and ARC scores official benchmark results?

They use pinned real test splits, with versioned zero-shot chat prompts and deterministic numeric/answer-letter grading. They are Wattever adaptations, not published few-shot or likelihood-based leaderboard protocols. Compare matching suite/subset, token budget, sampling and grading versions. Public tasks may be contaminated, and repeats are not independent questions. See [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

## Does a configuration fingerprint prove which model ran?

No. It checks consistency of public model/endpoint identifiers and known/requested/reported settings. A canonical ID helps distinguish a served alias, but hashes do not authenticate weights or server routing. Unknown effective reasoning, MTP or quantization remains unknown.

## Must I invent an endpoint name or ID?

No. Connect resolves them automatically, as do direct API starts. Names come from recognized official cloud hosts or explicit service metadata, with generic Local/Private/Remote endpoint fallbacks when unknown. Ports and model names are not used to guess software. Advanced settings offer one optional **Display name** override. Canonical known public API routes have stable provider IDs; other routes use a private random-ID registry without publishing or hashing the connection URL.

## Can telemetry show thermal throttling?

It shows observed utilization, temperatures, clocks and power where sensors exist. Whole-run aggregates and recent history can reveal changes to investigate. Different workloads and competing processes also change these readings; drift alone does not diagnose throttling. The bounded recent trace may omit older samples while whole-run observed means/peaks remain preserved.

---

## docs/troubleshooting.md

Canonical source: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md)

# Troubleshooting

- **Hosted page cannot connect:** check the endpoint URL, server availability, CORS and your browser's local-network permission. HTTPS-to-localhost behavior varies by browser. See [browser mode](docs/browser.md).
- **Browser storage warning:** download the result JSON before closing the page; an in-memory result is lost on reload.
- **A benchmark cannot be merged:** the merge dialog names the reason next to it. Benchmarks must come from one machine with the same GPU driver, corpus and protocol version, and must not be running. An endpoint benchmark saved as remote can join once you confirm that inference ran on the machine that launched it; one without a record of that machine cannot. Only one already merged benchmark can take part, and it stays the destination.
- **Helper endpoint discovery fails:** verify the API base URL and, if the endpoint requires one, the API key under **Connection options**. The key is never saved: enter it again after reloading the page or restarting the helper. Use a root URL or API base such as `/v1`, not `/chat/completions`. Enter the exact served model ID manually if `/models` is unavailable. Run a small case to verify streaming inference; CORS is not required for helper-to-engine requests. See [API configuration](docs/api.md).
- **Endpoint name is generic or unexpected:** the service did not expose recognized metadata, or only route-origin information is available. A generic Local/Private/Remote endpoint name is valid and does not block inference. Connect again after correcting the URL, or set the optional advanced **Display name** override. No manual ID is needed. A regenerated ID after clearing local storage or removing the private registry is expected; keep URL mappings private.
- **Generic endpoint throughput is unavailable:** check whether the provider includes prompt and completion token usage in its stream. Wattever keeps throughput unavailable when those counts are missing; stream chunks are not tokens. Inspect `metric_sources` and `reported_timings` in JSON.
- **Generic power is unavailable:** local power attribution is disabled by default. Confirm inference runs on this computer before checking that assertion; a loopback proxy alone does not establish local inference. Remote server power cannot be measured by client sensors.
- **Generic endpoint context failure or timeout:** reduce the workload or adjust context/KV allocation in the inference engine. Inspect the engine after cancellation or timeout; client abort does not verify server termination. Once the engine is idle, reconnect and choose **Continue this benchmark…** or **Add / rerun tests**.
- **A model was skipped on an endpoint:** the endpoint answered but refused that model, for the test and for a short check sent afterwards. The failed test is recorded as `model_unavailable` with the endpoint's own message, the model's remaining tests are skipped, and the other models run normally. A typical cause is a served ID that is not a chat model, such as a speculative-decoding drafter. Fix or remove the model, then use **Retry failed tests**.
- **The benchmark stopped because the endpoint stopped responding:** after a failed request the helper waits up to a minute for the endpoint to answer again. If it does not, or if it rejects the API key, the run stops and the tests that did not run stay unrecorded. Restart the inference server, reconnect, and choose **Continue this benchmark…**.
- **A managed test is very slow, or LM Studio shows only part of the model on the GPU:** the model did not load at the requested placement and **Use CPU memory if needed** loaded it with fewer GPU layers. The result's **Placement** (`gpu_offload`) reads `auto`, `0.5` or `off` instead of `max`. Reduce the prompt size or query count so the context fits in VRAM, or turn the option off to record the load as a failure. See [automatic fallbacks and substitutions](docs/measurements.md#automatic-fallbacks-and-substitutions).
- **Helper timeout recovery stopped:** inspect LM Studio and ensure the model and requests have stopped before starting another run. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

- **LM Studio or models unavailable:** install LM Studio, run `lms bootstrap`, start its server and check that the models are downloaded. Verify `LMS_BASE_URL` if using a different endpoint. Reopen Wattever and check the Run page.
- **Power unavailable:** check `nvidia-smi` for NVIDIA sensors. On macOS, use the launcher and accept the optional power prompt; without authorization speed tests still work. Other sensors may not provide power. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).
- **Load failure or context overflow:** reduce prompt size or simultaneous queries, inspect model context limits and available memory, or choose a smaller model. A failure is retained in results; use the retry option after correcting the cause.
- **Extension rejected:** extensions require matching hardware, selected GPU/driver and corpus. Managed LM Studio also checks its version; external repairs require reconnection to the saved endpoint. Start a separate benchmark if compatibility changed or cannot be verified. See [sessions](docs/measurements.md).
- **No response from Wattever:** check the URL printed by its launcher and keep the server window open. The default starting port is 8713 but another available port may be selected. See [getting started](docs/getting-started.md).
- **Updated files but old UI or API:** finish active work, restart the helper and reload the page. `/api/version` includes a `build_id`; matching release numbers alone do not establish a matching build. The launcher preserves active speed/capability runs and can replace only an identified idle older helper. Use its printed URL; do not stop the model server to refresh Wattever.
- **Browser disconnect / WinError 10053:** a closed or aborted browser connection does not establish a benchmark failure. The helper handles disconnects while sending headers/body; reconnect and inspect saved status/results before starting another run. Update/restart an idle helper if its request handler still prints a disconnect traceback.
- **Capability parameter rejected:** select **Provider default** to omit unsupported `reasoning_effort`, or choose the token-limit field the endpoint supports. A changed request protocol is a distinct comparison. No visible answer after a short budget may mean hidden reasoning consumed it; inspect the run's usage/finish reason and adjust budgets fairly.
- **Capability import rejected:** use a finished full audit file with matching public configuration/suite/protocol/subset hashes and unchanged answers/grades. Redacted responses cannot be independently re-scored. Completed files need all planned observations; partial work uses cancelled/error/interrupted status. Do not repair hashes to conceal edited measurements.
- **CPU temperature unavailable or history starts late:** CPU temperature needs an actual supported sensor and can be unavailable while GPU temperature works. On Windows, choose **Enable CPU temperature** in System and approve the administrator prompt; it installs the signed PawnIO driver and a read-only Wattever sensor task, and **Remove CPU sensor** undoes it. If the prompt was declined, nothing changed and the button stays available. Alternatively, start HWiNFO with Shared Memory Support enabled, or LibreHardwareMonitor with its remote web server on port 8085; the helper picks it up within seconds, without a restart. Wattever installs or elevates nothing unless you click the button. The System view states the reason a reading is missing. History retains the latest 3,600 points; check retention and all-run summary rather than interpreting absent samples as zero or no activity.

- **File-save warning:** review the warning's **Technical details** and retain downloaded JSON. For a managed LM Studio run, **Add / rerun tests → Add missing tests** can continue saved work after recovery. Generic endpoint runs start separately.

---

## CONTRIBUTING.md

Canonical source: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)

# Contributing

Share benchmark results by opening a pull request with one JSON file in `results/runs/`. The [sharing guide](docs/sharing-results.md) explains the GitHub upload workflow and how to add missing tests later. Review the file for information you do not want to publish and follow [results guidance](results/README.md). Record model builds, placement and relevant settings so readers can interpret results.

Capability contributions use individual `results/capabilities/<id>.json` files. Preserve full public audit answers, scorer decisions, suite/protocol/subset fingerprints and public configuration identities. Review prompts/expected answers and generated text before sharing. The helper's import independently re-scores and checks consistency; fingerprints do not authenticate execution. Keep dataset licenses/attribution and distinguish Wattever chat adaptations from official benchmark harnesses. See [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

For code changes, preserve old result readability, distinguish measured values from estimates, and document changes in measurement semantics. Wattever uses the Python standard library and local browser assets. See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [API](docs/api.md), [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and [security](SECURITY.md).

Run the software checks applicable to your change:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests
node --check web/app.js
node tests/test_ui.js
node tests/test_endpoint_ui.js
node tests/test_browser_backend.js
node tests/test_capabilities_ui.js
node tests/test_tables.js
python tools/validate_results.py
python tools/update_docs.py --check
```

The optional browser test is `node tests/test_ui_browser.cjs`. State which platforms and real hardware you exercised; software tests cannot establish GPU performance. Follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

---

## SECURITY.md

Canonical source: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)

# Security

The local helper rejects cross-origin state changes and non-loopback Host names. POST requests with a body require `Content-Type: application/json`; authenticated discovery uses `POST /api/endpoint/check`, not query parameters on GET. This prevents an unrelated webpage from asking the helper to forward named environment credentials. Command-line API clients without an Origin header remain supported.

Wattever serves a local interface that can start benchmarks, load or unload managed LM Studio models, and change local results. Keep it bound to loopback and use it only on a trusted machine. Generic endpoints receive your benchmark prompts and can incur provider charges; use a provider you trust.

An endpoint API key is typed into the helper's **Endpoint** card. It exists only in memory: in that field and in the running helper process. It travels in same-origin requests to the local helper and from there to the configured endpoint as a Bearer token; redirects are not followed, and a key is refused in a URL. It is never written to benchmark files, the saved form or exports, and it is removed from recorded endpoint errors, so it must be entered again after reloading the page. Scripts can name an environment variable instead (`endpoint_api_key_env`). Endpoint URLs, credential variable names and credentials are excluded from public results and exports. They are not a substitute for reviewing free text: labels, notes, model names, reproducibility fields and compute sources are public annotations. Do not put secrets or private server locations in them. Browser-mode keys remain in memory; see [browser privacy](docs/browser.md).

Hardware discovery uses read-only, allow-listed OS/driver fields without elevation. It excludes serial numbers, GPU UUIDs, hostnames, network addresses and user paths. Inventory describes the benchmark client; it does not authenticate a remote inference server or verify its hardware. Local-inference attribution is an explicit user assertion. Review exported JSON before sharing, including older imported results that may contain legacy identifiers.

Capability audit files preserve exact public suite prompts, expected answers and source citations so their dataset digests and grading can be checked. Review those materials and generated answers before publication. Privacy-redacted responses cannot be imported as full independently scored audits. Public model/endpoint IDs must not contain connection locations or secrets. Content fingerprints establish consistency, not authentication or evidence that particular weights were served; see [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

Canonical known public API routes use stable public provider IDs. Other automatic identities use random public route IDs with private URL mappings in ignored `results/.endpoint-routes.json` or browser local storage. Do not publish those mappings. The System history log in ignored `results/.telemetry/` records this computer's load, memory, power and temperatures for the last 24 hours; it stays local and is never part of results, exports or Share. Connection URLs are not hashed into public IDs or result fingerprints. Service detection and route-origin labels are evidence about the connection, not verification of remote inference hardware or backend weights. Optional display names remain public annotations and need review.

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to the repository maintainers through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting if available. Do not publish sensitive details before maintainers can respond. See [API](docs/api.md) for state-changing endpoints.

---

## CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Canonical source: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

# Code of conduct

Treat participants with respect. Be constructive, welcome differing experience levels, and avoid harassment, discrimination and personal attacks. Maintainers may remove inappropriate contributions or limit participation to protect the community. Report concerns privately to the repository maintainers through GitHub. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## CHANGELOG.md

Canonical source: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Adds an optional **Enable CPU temperature** button to System on Windows when no CPU temperature is readable. After one administrator approval it installs the signed PawnIO driver (2.2.0) and a read-only Wattever task that reads only the CPU package thermal registers (Intel `IA32_PACKAGE_THERM_STATUS`, AMD Tctl); readings carry `cpu_temp_source` `windows_wattever_pawnio:intel_package` or `:amd_tctl`. Both downloads are pinned by SHA-256 and checked again in the administrator-only install folder before anything runs. **Remove CPU sensor** deletes the task and its files and uninstalls PawnIO only if Wattever installed it. `GET`/`POST /api/system/cpu-sensor` report and start the setup.
- Adds the [vLLM on two RTX 5070 Ti cards](docs/vllm-two-5070-ti.md) study with two Wattever runs of NVIDIA's NVFP4 Qwen3.8-27B served by vLLM, a long-prompt sweep, a prefix-reuse probe and per-batch energy against LM Studio.
- Reads CPU temperature on Windows from a sensor tool that is already running: HWiNFO (Shared Memory Support) or LibreHardwareMonitor (web server) for the CPU package, otherwise Core Temp (hottest core) or a live ACPI thermal zone, each named in `cpu_temp_source` and in the System view. Nothing is installed or elevated, and no value is estimated: a thermal zone that never changes is treated as a placeholder. When no source exists, `cpu_temp_note` and the System view say why, instead of an empty CPU temperature line. Previously Windows never reported CPU temperature.
- Reworks the **Results this run** table in Benchmarks: the title shows the average batch wall time, prefill time and speed, and decode time and speed over the tests that completed, each in the colour that underlines its column; the header stays in place while the rows scroll inside the table; the Status column is removed and a failed test is drawn in red with its reason. The explanation of decode timing moves under the table.
- Moves the MTP speculative decoding choice (**Off**, **On**, **Compare both**) out of the collapsed Advanced settings into the Workload card of Benchmarks. The choice can always be made, and the benchmark resolves whether a model can be launched with MTP: a model LM Studio loads is tried and its MTP pass skipped when it has no MTP head. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint decides MTP itself, so **Compare both** runs its standard pass and records that the MTP pass was not run, and **On** alone says why nothing can run instead of starting. Previously the choice disappeared for endpoints.
- Recognizes LM Studio on this computer when it is entered as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`http://localhost:1234/v1`, the computer's own network address or name) and connects it as **LM Studio (managed)**, so context, GPU placement and MTP can be set and models show their quantization. The Endpoint card says so and offers **Use as a plain endpoint instead**. That choice is remembered for the address until LM Studio (managed) is connected by hand. An address with an API key stays an endpoint. `POST /api/endpoint/check` reports this as `helper_lmstudio`.
- Keeps the chosen prompt lengths, simultaneous queries, repeats, answer length and MTP mode when you click **Connect**. Previously connecting reset them.
- Reopens Benchmarks on LM Studio when LM Studio was the last connection made in this browser. Previously the page reopened on the endpoint of the last benchmark, even when that endpoint was no longer running.
- Records System telemetry continuously while the helper runs, whether or not System is open, and keeps a rolling last-24-hours log on this computer in the gitignored `results/.telemetry/` (one file per hour, finished hours compressed, older ones deleted). Opening System shows what happened while nobody watched; windows extend to 24 hours, **Earlier**/**Later** and **Go to time** reach any moment in the last day, and long windows average readings while the readout keeps the peak. Axes, the readout and the status line show local clock times, with the date when it is not today, instead of "s ago" or "s old". The monitor no longer stops after 15 seconds without a viewer; during a benchmark it reads the benchmark's sampler instead of running a second sensor stream. New route: `/api/system/history`.
- Accepts an endpoint API key typed directly into the helper's Endpoint card, replacing the environment-variable name. The key stays in memory, is sent only to that endpoint, and is never written to benchmark files, the saved form, exports or recorded errors. The API field is `endpoint_api_key`; `endpoint_api_key_env` remains for scripts.
- Merges benchmarks of one machine from Results: tick them and choose **Merge into one…**, or follow the **Same machine** suggestion. The helper recognizes the machine, including for endpoint benchmarks saved as remote, names every reason a benchmark cannot join, and asks for confirmation before attributing an endpoint benchmark to the machine that launched it. Benchmarks of one engine can now be merged, a test measured more than once keeps its completed, most recent measurement with the others archived, and **Undo merge** restores the original files exactly. New routes: `/api/bench/merge-plan`, `/api/bench/merge-suggestions` and `/api/bench/merge-undo`.
- Keeps an endpoint benchmark running when the endpoint cannot serve one of its models. After a failed request the helper checks the endpoint: a model it refuses is recorded as `model_unavailable`, its remaining tests are skipped and the other models still run. Only an endpoint that stops responding, rejects the key or cannot be checked stops the run, with the unmeasured tests left to continue. Previously any failed request ended the whole benchmark.
- Fixes **Connect** with Provider set to LM Studio reporting "LM Studio has no models indexed" when the last benchmark used an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that is no longer running. The helper listed that endpoint's models instead of LM Studio's; Connect now asks for LM Studio's catalog with `/api/env?provider=lmstudio`.
- Fixes **Add / rerun tests** on endpoint benchmarks saved as remote, which were always refused for a differing GPU. A stopped benchmark offers **Continue this benchmark…** under its progress bar.
- Folds notices in Results and under the progress bar into one slim strip, collapsed by default, that says what needs attention and unfolds to the details. A test that did not pass shows its reason in the live results table, and chart tooltips no longer cut benchmark names.
- Boxes similar models together in the Results model list: the same model under different publishers, quantizations or engines, then one family in several sizes. A box header shows or hides all of its models, and **only** selects just that box.
- Replaces the Recorded conditions panel with switches in the chart key: click a benchmark there to hide or show its curves. Entries that are on carry a faint wash of their own colour; all are on by default.
- Organizes the interface into System, Benchmarks, Results, Capabilities and Share, with independent local system monitoring.
- Replaces the Results Summary with an Overview of each model's peak prefill and decode speed, its change across prompt length and concurrent queries, and the longest prompt completed. Any figure opens its graph.
- Rebuilds Graphs & comparisons around a toggle-button control panel with no menus: several metrics at once, prompt length or concurrent queries on the axis, several query counts or prompt lengths as separate lines, model toggles, and colour by model or benchmark. Charts gain a compare-at-pointer tooltip and a shared key that highlights its lines.
- Stops failed or skipped tests from appearing as separate recorded conditions, and names a condition as a variant only when another one measured the same model. Provenance labels and a session's test plan no longer split one model into several configurations.
- Accounts for every passed test in Graphs: a banner states how many the current toggles draw and offers one-click remedies for the rest, each chart names the values it could not draw and why, and untouched defaults choose query counts, metrics and colours that show everything while the chart stays readable. Library cards say "N tests passed" and list the model count.
- Reports complete concurrent-batch prefill and output rates using recorded batch timing, while preserving per-request evidence and unavailable timing.
- Documents the Samsung 990 PRO GLM-5.3-Flash tuning campaign with separate native/client phase timings, memory/cache telemetry, long retrieval, frozen accuracy screens and ranked upgrade options; the higher-quant comparison remains in progress.

- Retains requested MTP metadata for external endpoints, separately from effective settings and observed per-request draft counts. This annotation does not configure the inference server.
- Retries transient permission failures during atomic capability-result saves, preserving completed answers without repeating model requests. Other persistence failures retain a non-sensitive error type.

- Supports atomic cancellation of an owned speed or capability run using an expected run ID, and identifies endpoints that explicitly report Project Maya.
- Keeps capability collection separate from fresh RAM, storage and CUDA transfer probes; unavailable or reused hardware evidence retains its provenance.

- Displays planned but unrecorded cases in consolidated comparison views.

- Identifies endpoints automatically, discovers Results models from the current authenticated connection, and records model, quantization, reasoning and MTP provenance. Public exports omit connection addresses and credentials; unknown effective settings remain explicit.
- Adds capability evaluation with original Core tasks and pinned GSM8K and AI2 ARC-Challenge test splits. Zero-shot chat adaptations retain prompts, answers, grading evidence, subsets and repeats; they are separate from official leaderboard scores. Capability generation has an independent thinking-and-answer budget.

- Records each detected NVIDIA card and simultaneous combined power, energy, VRAM and utilization. Concurrent requests share one energy interval. Live telemetry also shows CPU/RAM load, available temperatures and clocks, with measurement scope, missing values and retention coverage.
- Adds CPU, memory-topology, storage and per-card PCIe/transfer metadata, including native RAM copies, storage reads and pinned host-to-GPU probes. Hardware and transfer cards distinguish measured, inferred, saved and unavailable observations.
- Organizes Results into Summary, Table and Compare. Selected metrics have individual graphs; shared filters expose recorded storage and engine conditions, quantization methods, matching cases and raw repeats.
- Consolidates compatible engine sessions into one benchmark per hardware setup while preserving measurements and source metadata. Recorded board identities prevent incompatible board combinations. Same-file additions, repairs and removals retain backups and attempt history.
- Shows completed, stopped, failed and incomplete states explicitly. Preserves active work during helper refreshes, handles disconnected browsers, and blocks new tests while outstanding client requests are still closing after a timeout.
- Publishes five consolidated hardware comparisons, covering the RTX 5060 Ti, ASUS Prime and PNY RTX 5070 Ti boards, the i7-5820K/i7-5960X CPU comparison, and the mixed dual-GPU setup. Storage alternatives retain their measured baselines.
- Adds a separate dual-GPU communication and execution study with reproducible configurations, source fingerprints, raw samples, per-card energy and metric-specific graphs. Profiling and diagnostic captures remain separate from normal benchmark aggregates.
- Updates the portable release, hosted result catalog, documentation and API operator skill for the endpoint, capability and multi-GPU workflows.

## 2.4.0 - 2026-10-27

- Adds adaptive request deadlines and verified model unload and worker recovery before continuing after a timeout.
- Adds a documentation set and an agent skill for the local API.

- Older result schemas and planner settings remain readable. Extended files may contain sessions using different planners; compare provenance and settings before combining measurements.
